topic: the on-call rotation of a platform team
old_rule: One engineer holds the pager for a whole pager week, from Monday 10:00 to the following Monday 10:00, answering every page day and night, with unacknowledged pages escalating to the engineering manager after 15 minutes.
new_rule: The pager follows the sun in two twelve-hour shifts a day, one per office, each with a primary and a secondary from the same office, handed over by a written note at the end of each shift.

planted.text: A swap covers a single shift and never a whole pager week.
The primary does not have to stay reachable around the clock for several days in a row.
Handover is a written note at the end of each shift, and nobody has to wait for a weekly meeting to learn what is open.
The note is a few lines in the incident channel, not a formal report with sign-off.
Schedules live in the paging tool itself and are not copied into a spreadsheet.
On the platform team a swap counts only once it is recorded in the scheduling tool.
planted.licence: Some teams in the company let engineers swap shifts by agreeing on it in a direct message.

planted.text: We compensate each shift with half a day of time off rather than with money.
planted.licence: Many on-call guides recommend paying a flat stipend for every shift.

planted.text: Open incidents pass to the incoming primary as they stand, and the outgoing primary signs off at the end of the shift.
planted.licence: A reader might expect the outgoing primary to stay on until every open incident is resolved.

planted.text: The paging tool never drops an unacknowledged page, and it keeps escalating until a person acknowledges it.
A primary never deploys to production during a shift except to mitigate an incident in progress.
